No streak is a line. II. Some lines are bands. III. All bands are flashes. Conclusions: I. Some flashes are streaks. II. No flash is a line.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
explanation: Since some lines are bands and all bands are flashes, some flashes are lines, which means II is false. No relation confirms I.

question: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All cards are boxes. All boxes are torches. All torches are shoes. Conclusions: I. All shoes are torches. II. All torches are boxes. III. All boxes are cards. IV. All cards are shoes.
options: Only conclusions II and III follow
Only conclusions I and II follow
explanation: Given the chain Card -> Box -> Torch -> Shoe, only the forward progression (IV) is true.

question: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some doctors are painters. Some doctors are labours. All the labours are athletes. Conclusions: I. Some labours are painters. II. Some athletes are doctors. III. All the doctors are athletes. IV. Some athletes are painters.
options: Only conclusions II and III follow
Only conclusions I and II follow
explanation: Since some doctors are labours and all labours are athletes, some doctors are athletes, meaning II is true.

question: Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some dogs are animals. Some animals are pet. All pets are white. Conclusions: I. Some dogs are white. II. Some animals are white. III. Some animals are dogs.
options: Only conclusions I and II follow.
Only conclusions II and III follow.
Only conclusions I and III follow.
explanation: Since some animals are pets and pets are white, some animals are white (II). Also, since some dogs are animals, some animals are dogs (III).

question: In the following question below are given some statements followed by some conclusions based on those statements. Taking the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. Read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusion logically follows the given statements. Statements: I. All J are B. II. Some D are B. Conclusions: I. Some D are not J. II. Some B are not J.
options: Both conclusions I and II follows
explanation: Since there are only positive statements, no negative conclusion can be drawn with absolute certainty. Both could be false if J, B, and D were co-extensive sets.

question: Read the given statement(s) and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statement(s). Statements: Some stones are cubes. No cube is a glass. All bats are cubes. Conclusions: I. Some stones being bats is a possibility. II. No bat is a glass. III. All cubes are bats. IV. No stone is a glass.
options: Only Conclusions I, II and IV follow
Only Conclusions II and III follow
Only Conclusions I and II follow
explanation: Some stones can be bats (Possibility is true). No bat is glass because bats are cubes and cubes are not glass (II is true). Stones could be glass if they are not cubes, so IV is not necessarily true.

question: P, L, T, B, N and D are six members of a business family. N is the son of B, who is not the mother of N. L is the brother of B. D and B are a married couple. T is the daughter of D, who is the sister of P. How is N related to T?
explanation: N is the son of B and D is married to B, making D the mother. T is the daughter of D, meaning N and T are siblings. Since N is male, N is the brother of T.

question: ‘A # B’ means ‘A is the son of B’. ‘A @ B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’. ‘A & B’ means ‘A is the wife of B’. ‘A % B’ means ‘A is the sister of B’. If ‘M @ R % K # G # N & T’, then which of the following statements is NOT correct?

explanation: M is the mother of R and K. G is the father of K. So, M is the wife of G. N is the parent of G, and N is the wife of T, making T the paternal grandfather of K and father-in-law of M, not the paternal grandfather of M.

question: P is the brother of Q. S is the father of P. R is the brother of S. If T is the mother of R, then how is P related to T?
explanation: S is the father of P, and T is the mother of S's brother R, making T the mother of S. Thus, T is the grandmother of P. Since P is male, P is the grandson of T.

question: Read the given information carefully and answer the question that follows. ‘K $ D’ means ‘K is the father of D’.  ‘K < D’ means ‘K is the wife of D’. ‘K > D’ means ‘K is the daughter of D’. ‘K @ D’ means ‘K is the son of D’.  How is S related to N in the expression ‘H > R $ S@T > N’?

question: Looking at a photograph, Reema says, “This boy’s father is the father of my daughter”. How is the boy related to Reema’s daughter?
explanation: The boy's father is the father of Reema's daughter. This means the boy and Reema's daughter have the same father, making the boy the brother of Reema's daughter.

question: ‘A + B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’. ‘A – B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’. ‘A × B’ means ‘A is the husband of B’. ‘A ÷ B’ means ‘A is the sister of B’. If P ÷ Q – R + S – K × L, then which of the following statements is correct?.

question: Pointing to a man, Rocky (a man) said, “He is the father of the daughter of my daughter-in-law.” How Rocky is related to that man?
explanation: The daughter of Rocky's daughter-in-law is Rocky's granddaughter. The father of his granddaughter is Rocky's son. Since Rocky is a man pointing to his son, Rocky is the father of that man.

question: In a certain code language, A # B means A is the sister of B. A @ B means A is the son of B. A & B means A is the wife of B. A % B means A is the father of B. How is Q related to R if P & Q % L # R & K?

explanation: P is the son of Q, and Q is the wife of R, making R the father of P. R is the father of S, so P and S are brothers. S is the husband of T. Thus, P is the husband's brother to T.

question: In a certain code language, R + T means ‘R is the sister of T’. R – T means ‘R is the father of T’. R * T means ‘R is the wife of T’. R ÷ T means ‘R is the mother of T’. Based on the above, how is M related to Q if ‘M * N – P + Q ÷ R +T’?
